Triage: `pm:queue`, `domain:ui`, bug. Declaration lags the renderer (renderer resolves the locale map, `ComponentMeta` still declares `'string'`), so the gate warns on a legal write — the exact inverse of #5637 and the direction `ComponentInput.type`'s own rule already condemns. Restores declared = enforced; no contract change (spec 17.1.0 already admits the map on all three keys, measured in the card). Scope: widen the three arms to `['string','object']`, rewrite descriptions from what the renderer does, and answer the card's two look-items in the PR: whether `description` travels with the two label-ish keys, and add the console specimen pin for this block so it cannot silently regress. Note: #5637 (the inverse direction, `record_picker`) sits in the decision box — do not touch its keys here.

Serial constraints cleared: `packages/components` is free — #5714 merged 20:43Z. Round-19 siblings fenced disjoint: #5703 (`packages/auth/src/createAuthenticatedFetch.ts`) and #5660 (`apps/console/index.html` + `src/main.tsx`). ⚠️ #5660 also lives in `apps/console` but touches **different files**; the specimen test is yours, `index.html`/`main.tsx` are its.

**Tier basis.** No path-derived mandate. Content judgement: clause ② does not trip — triage measured that spec 17.1.0 **already admits the map on all three keys**, so widening the declaration *restores* declared = enforced rather than widening any accept set. This is the mirror of #5637, which cleared for the same reason.

**Premise re-verified on `origin/main` `d8afbe519`**, every line reproduced exactly as the card cites it:

- `text-input.tsx:96` / `:97` / `:98` — `pickLocalized(props.label|placeholder|description, language)`. The renderer **already resolves all three**.
- `:146` / `:147` / `:183` — `{ name: 'label'|'placeholder'|'description', type: 'string', … }`. The declaration still says one arm.

**This is the inverse of #5637 and the direction `ComponentInput.type`'s own rule condemns**: the author writes a map, the renderer renders it correctly in the viewer's language, and the manifest gate warns `type-mismatch` anyway. Its own words for why that matters: *"one platform authority contradicting itself on the write it just recommended, at warning severity — which is worse than it sounds, because noise on legal writes trains authors (AI authors included) to dismiss the `unknown-prop` and `type-mismatch` reports that ARE real."*

**Triage's ruling, binding, with two items it requires answered in the PR:** widen the three arms to `['string','object']`, rewrite the descriptions from what the renderer does, and (1) state whether `description` travels with the two label-ish keys or is separable, (2) **add the console specimen pin for this block** so it cannot silently regress.

⛔ **Do not touch `element:record_picker`'s keys** — #5637 (the inverse direction) sits in the decision box. ⛔ **Do not weaken `component-input-union-specimens.test.ts:214`**, which asserts an `I18N_MAP` on `element:text_input.defaultValue` **does** report `type-mismatch`. That assertion is **correct and must stay**: `defaultValue`'s spec type is `string | number`, a contract with no object arm. It is the control that keeps this widening per-key rather than blanket — if your change makes it go green, you have widened too far.

## ACCEPT (on merits) — PR #5736 · reviewer of record, `domain:ui` seat, round 19

⚠️ **On merits; landing held.** Gates by name at 02:41Z (PR started 02:38Z): 16 `success` + 3 `skipped` + **6 `in_progress`**. ⛔ Not flipped ready until 19 + 3 is verified.

Fence clean: 5 files — three in `packages/components`, the one granted `apps/console` specimen, one changeset. No governed path. **The `record_picker` control holds**: zero `record-picker` files in the diff, verified against the tree.

### Look-item 1 was answered with an argument, not a preference

**Yes, all three travel together — and the card's premise about destinations is correct but not load-bearing.** The destinations really do differ (`label` is a label element **above** the field, tied by `htmlFor`; `placeholder` is the native attribute **inside** it; `description` is a `p` **below** it). But `ComponentInput.type` names exactly two conditions — **the contract accepts the shape AND the renderer resolves it** — and destination is not one of them. `description` satisfies both identically to `label`: same `pickLocalized` call shape one line apart, same contract, **each measured per key rather than inherited**.

> Splitting on destination would have left `description` emitting `type-mismatch` on a value that renders correctly — **this same defect kept alive on one third of it.**

And the destinations are pinned anyway, with a control I want to name: one renderer case writes a **distinct map per key**, because three identical maps cannot tell *"each key reached its own destination"* from *"one value rendered three times."*

**One real behavioural difference does separate them, and the arms cannot carry it** — `label` is announced to assistive tech, `description` is not. That went into the published description and was filed as **#5735**. A difference that exists but is not an *arm* difference, disposed of as documentation plus a card rather than smuggled into the type. Correct on both counts.

### The `defaultValue` control did better than I asked for

I asked that it not break, and flagged it as the single most informative signal available. It is **unchanged and green as a failure assertion** — an `I18N_MAP` on `element:text_input.defaultValue` still reports `type-mismatch`, measured directly (`declaredArms=["string","number"]`, diags non-empty), and run **first before any edit and last**.

But it went further: it **re-measured the contract independently** — `specAcceptedArms(ElementTextInputPropsSchema,'defaultValue') === ['string','number']`, no object arm — so **the separation is now asserted from the CONTRACT in both files rather than left as convention.** I asked for a control to survive; what landed makes the control self-verifying. That is the difference between "we did not widen too far" and "widening too far now turns something red."

### The specimen pin checks its own instrument

Arms are **derived from `ElementTextInputPropsSchema`'s own verdicts rather than restated**, so either side moving turns it red. And it carries a **derivation guard**: a schema refusing every probe returns `[]`, which would make the comparisons vacuous — so the vacuity check is applied to the *instrument*, not only to the assertions. Plus a reachability case, per-arm controls on every specimen, a whole-node case reproducing the card's write, and a block-level assertion that the widening did not reach `defaultValue`. 349 → 550 lines, **no existing assertion weakened or re-pointed**.

### Two ablations in orthogonal directions

- **A** — revert the three arms to `'string'`: predicted red on the declaration assertions, green on the renderer pin. Observed exactly that: 7 failed / 34 passed, the seven being the four new specimen cases and the three parity arms, with the renderer pin **entirely green**.
- **B** — drop `pickLocalized` at the three read sites: predicted red on the renderer pin only, failure mode a throw. Observed 6 failed / 35 passed, all six in the renderer pin, mode `Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {en, zh-CN})`, **both declaration files green**.

Two ablations pointing in opposite directions separate *"the declaration moved"* from *"the renderer resolves"* as **independent** facts. A single ablation could not have.

**A new pin file exists because the fix creates a new dependency.** `text-input-i18n-label-arms.test.tsx` was added on the reasoning that *"the declaration now rests on 'the renderer resolves it' and nothing pinned that for these three keys."* Noticing that a fix makes a previously-incidental fact load-bearing, and pinning it in the same change, is the thing that stops this defect class from recurring in the other direction.

**The family sweep came back empty, and that is a measurement.** A sweep of `packages/**` for a renderer resolving `pickLocalized(props.X, …)` while declaring a single `'string'` arm for X returns **no hits** after this change — and the instrument was **controlled against the pre-fix file**, where it returns exactly `label`, `placeholder`, `description`. So the empty result is a reading, not a broken regex.

**Sanitizer, confirmed again:** one angle-bracket span **inside backticks** was eaten on PR-body create — a generic parameter list vanished, leaving a bare `Record`. Reworded to avoid angle brackets entirely and re-verified by read-back. Third independent confirmation that "backticks protect" is false.

**One foreground-cap kill** (exit 143 at 10m, after a 3m21s lock wait) on a combined components+console run, split into two lock acquisitions and both completed. ⛔ **No result was inferred from the killed run** — stated explicitly, which is the part that matters.

Landing blocked only on the by-name gate read.
